narration: Welcome to the Sculpture Gallery, where we have a beautiful Seated Buddha, accession number NM 62.2/6, carved in the 5th‑century Gupta style from the characteristic spotted red sandstone of Mathura. The figure sits in meditation with the earth‑touching gesture, a calm, idealised form that reflects the Gupta era’s shift from earlier flamboyance to serene refinement. Standing 70 centimetres tall, it features a simple halo that echoes the restrained elegance of Gupta iconography. This piece was acquired by the National Museum as part of its Gupta sculpture collection, and it reminds us how a single stone can carry the spiritual quietude of an entire age.
